query: Why is chunk overlap used in the RAG pipeline?
answer: Chunk overlap is used in the RAG pipeline to maintain context across split text chunks (typically using an overlap of 10-20% of the chunk size).

notes.detail: [search] q="chunk overlap RAG pipeline" | RELEVANT x1 / MARGINAL x0 | best d=0.285 (docs/rag_guide.md) | excerpt: # RAG Architecture Guide  ## What is RAG? Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines information retrieval with text generation. It grounds LLM responses in factual, retrieved documents.  ## RAG Pipeline Components  ### 1. Document Ingestion - Load documents from various sources (PDF, TXT, MD, etc.) - Extract text content - Clean and normalize text  ### 2. Chunking - Split documents into smaller, overlapping chunks - Typical chunk size: 256-1024 tokens - Overlap: 10-20% of chunk size to maintain context
